answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity, not names. Before a wallet may vote or grade it must bond stake at a public inlet: an address whose history is replayable. Flooding the ledger with ten thousand fakes then means funding ten thousand bonds, each bearing a fee, before one tally moves. Reputation settles like silt behind a jetty, weighted by how long value stayed locked; a fresh wallet stays weightless, a faint nebula no tally can spend. Rewards unlock only after independent non-kin peers countersign the work, so each fake identity ends up subsidizing the honest operator.
